channel.title: Chaotic Good Computing
channel.description: Last 40 notes on Chaotic Good Computing

item.title: On Dead Math and Small Pickles
item.description: To understand why OpenAI completely upended the world of mathematics with its proof that Navier-Stokes is not smooth in three dimensions, you must first understand that cucumbers of any size can be properly pickled.

item.title: The Season of Stamps
item.description: The kickoff post for my Season of Stamps: exploring new places, meeting new people, and putting the final stamp of approval on a back catalog of projects worth publishing.

item.title: Chipotleware
item.description: A brief side-rant about the (former) burrito-style economics of junior-level software engineering

item.title: Software Gardening
item.description: Garden-inspired development as a non-sinister, people-centric way to think about post-LLM software development

item.title: Security Alert: Softlock and ACE via Natural Language Overload
item.description: I think I’ve found a pretty large CVE that has gone without a formal report, despite absolutely saturating the field of software engineering. It’s subtle and…

item.title: Lean Software Development: Prelude Notes
item.description: Notes on the prelude chapters of Lean Software Development (2003)

item.title: Working with Valves: Understanding the Structure of "Flat" Organizations
item.description: Many an engineer has heard tales of Valve's "flat" organization structure — what is fact, what is fiction, and how does it actually work? An annotated copy of the 2012 First Edition of Valve's Employee Handbook.

item.title: The Theory of Stupidity (and the graph inside you)
item.description: Our lives are all dominated by a little graph in our hearts — and sometimes, that graph gets wacky. A review of Dietrich Bonhoeffer's "Theory of Stupidity", part of his larger ~1943-1945 work "Letters and Papers from Prison."

item.title: Design of a mucin-selective protease for targeted degradation of cancer-associated mucins
item.description: The rubber hits the road on ColabFold! I hope that's rubber I'm smelling — although it may be the computer. A replication attempt of a protein fold figure in K. Pedram et al (2023).

item.title: An Annotated Guide to Hobbyist Protein Folding
item.description: Amaze (or bore) your friends and family by picking up on a hot new hobby that's all the rage — protein folding! An annotated starter to the 2021 paper "ColabFold - Making protein folding accessible to all"

item.title: Agentic Programming as Theory Building
item.description: Do humans have a role in software development anymore? Absolutely — but we need to rethink what it means to program. An modern review of Peter Naur's 1985 essay "Programming as Theory Building"

item.title: APL: Pattern 4; Agricultural Valleys
item.description: Urban development has the high ground over agricultural and ecological preservation — and it should! *A Pattern Language* annotations on Pattern 4: Agricultural Valleys

item.title: APL: Pattern 5; Lace of Country Streets
item.description: How dense is too dense? How sparse is too sparse? Annotations for A Pattern Language's proposals for the density of metro-adjacent country streets for agriculture, recreation, and preservation.

item.title: APL: Pattern 1; Independent Regions
item.description: Home isn't where the heart is — it's a single node on a very, very large graph. Annotations for the "Independent Regions" pattern of *A Pattern Language*.

item.title: APL: Pattern 2; The Distribution of Towns
item.description: How close is too close? How far is too far? *A Pattern Language* annotations related to the statistical, economic, and ecologic concerns in balancing how dense human habitats ought to be.

item.title: APL: Pattern 3; City Country Fingers
item.description: City, with natural stripes — or nature, with city stripes? Annotations for A Pattern Language, and tracking public opinion of where Americans want to live over the past 50 years.

item.title: APL: Pattern 0; Introduction
item.description: Can graphs be libertarian? Authoritarian? Annotations for the introductory portion of the 1977 book A Pattern Language.

item.title: Ants in the Neighborhood
item.description: Is Jane Street run by soccer-loving ants? Inconclusive. We *can* conclude that they're fans of Markov Chains, though — an invaluable tool for understanding complex data structures.

item.title: A Pattern Language, and a Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood
item.description: The beginning of a topological review of the 1977 urban design and architecture reference book A Pattern Language, and a journey to understand Earth's greatest graph: the Earth, itself.

item.title: Evolution and Revolution as Organizations Grow
item.description: Annotations for Greiner's 1972 paper "Evolution and Revolution as Organizations Grow", about the structural composition of organizations at different sizes and requirements.

item.title: Quick Fix: Tone Down Obsidian List/Header Padding
item.description: Annoyed by Obsidian Live Preview over-padding headers and aggressively indenting? Some snippets to help keep your notes from jumping around, so you can focus on actually writing them.

item.title: Dice Roll Distribution Widget
item.description: Discover the probability distributions of different dice roll combinations

item.title: The Advantages of Advantage: Intro to Probability Convolutions
item.description: What *is* the advantage of rolling with advantage? Exploring dice roll combinations and probability convolutions.

item.title: Quartz Widgets: Graphs, Galore!
item.description: I killed 4 of my blogs trying to implement MDX support. Will this one be next? Using MDX with Quartz to create interactive graphs, diagrams, and demos — clear as day.

item.title: LLMs; or, How to Run Your Own Hostage Negotiation
item.description: LLMs: Are we doomed to die, or born to garden? I'd like to make the case that AI is less like Terminator, and more like tomatoes.

item.title: Intro to Event Storming
item.description: Notes from learning Event Storming for domain-driven design. Thoughts on phases, color-coded chaos, and how to transition from fast pitches to full products.

item.title: Kickoff: Season of Systems
item.description: I'm learning to live with the systems that stole my beloved em-dash. A season dedicated to negotiating how to live with the agentic models that have turned my career upside-down.

item.title: Review: Season of Rhythm
item.description: Looking back at my year-long attempt to build up long-lasting habits. A retrospective on routines, remote work transitions, and learning the art of slow-and-steady.

item.title: LLMs: A Primer Presentation for Our Newest, Scariest Tool
item.description: An engineer-focused primer on the mechanisms that drive Large Language Models. Basics on how we got here, how they work, and how to use them without feeling an apocalyptic dread.

item.title: Typst Resume Template
item.description: A beginner-friendly resume template in Typst — 100% less LaTeX, 100% more opinions.

item.title: Terraform LocalStack Testing
item.description: $70/mo/seat? Just using live AWS may be cheaper. An evaluation of LocalStack as a testbed for Account Factory Terraform.

item.title: The Simple Economics of Open Source
item.description: Why do we do what we do? "Egoboo." Exploring economic models of OSS contributions beyond altruism and ego.

item.title: College Admissions and the Stability of Marriage
item.description: A dive into the hottest algorithm of the 1960s: Gale-Shapley matchmaking. Who knew that the mysteries of the heart could be solved with a matrix?

item.title: Feeling Right, Nothing Done: Don't Be the Death of Consensus
item.description: Classifying opinions as "strong" or "weak" to stop wasting hours in fruitless engineering debates. How consensus can beat being "right", and an open letter for the tactically apathetic.

item.title: Before You Slabtop Your Laptop: A Brief Warning
item.description: PSA: Check if your laptop needs an LCD for POST before removing the screen. Learned this the hard way after 5 hours and a fried motherboard. Learn from my dumb mistakes.

item.title: GPTinglish: Unnatural Language Processing
item.description: The only market crashing is the market for sanitized language. Stay human. Embrace typos.

item.title: Turning SelfControl into Self Restraint
item.description: Building a Raycast plugin to schedule website blocks — because checking news "just one more time" destroys flow. Automate SelfControl and self control: take your laptop back.

item.title: Caveat Lector: Reader Beware
item.description: I'm embracing being wrong on the internet in an effort to learn in public. A disclaimer on digital gardening, dead pixels, and the fear of terminal online-ness.

item.title: Some initial thoughts about time tracking
item.description: TODO.

item.title: The Quest to Slay The Goblin
item.description: My life devolves into sleep-eat-procrastinate cycles without structure—I call this "The Goblin." Productivity tools, hating on hustle culture, and a new definition for horticulture.
